back: A financial report showing a company's performance over a period of time.
It summarizes revenues and expenses to arrive at net income or loss.
Also called a profit and loss (P&L) statement.
$$\text{Gross Profit} = \text{Net Sales} - \text{Cost of Goods Sold}$$
It measures profitability before operating expenses.
A higher gross profit margin indicates better pricing and cost control.
cards.front: What is the formula for [[kw:gross profit]]?

back: Total sales revenue minus returns, allowances, and discounts.
$$\text{Net Sales} = \text{Gross Sales} - \text{Returns and Allowances}$$
It represents the actual revenue the company keeps.
The direct cost of merchandise sold during the period.
COGS = Beginning Inventory + Purchases – Ending Inventory.
It is subtracted from net sales to get gross profit.

cards.front: Calculate COGS: Beginning inventory $10,000, purchases $40,000, ending inventory $12,000.

back: Costs incurred to run the business that are not directly tied to production.
Examples: salaries, rent, utilities, advertising, depreciation.
They are subtracted from gross profit to arrive at operating income.

cards.front: How do you find [[kw:net income]] on an income statement?
back: $$\text{Net Income} = \text{Gross Profit} - \text{Operating Expenses}$$
If operating expenses exceed gross profit, the result is a net loss.
It is the bottom line of the income statement.
Expresses each item as a percentage of net sales.
$$\text{Percent of Sales} = \frac{\text{Line Item}}{\text{Net Sales}} \times 100$$
Allows comparison of cost structures across companies and periods.
cards.front: What is [[kw:vertical analysis]] of an income statement?

back: Sales is the top line that generates all revenue; it represents 100%.
All expenses and profit are compared to this base to show their relative weight.
It standardizes comparisons regardless of company size.
cards.front: Why is net sales used as the base for vertical analysis of the income statement?

back: Compares line items across two periods, showing dollar and percent changes.
$$\text{Percent Change} = \frac{\text{New} - \text{Old}}{\text{Old}} \times 100$$
Reveals trends in revenue, costs, and profit over time.
cards.front: What is [[kw:horizontal analysis]] of an income statement?
If sales grew 10% but operating expenses grew 25%, what does that indicate?
back: Expenses are rising faster than revenue, which squeezes profit margins.
Management should investigate the cause of the rising expenses.
It could signal inefficiency or lack of cost control.
Net profit margin = (Net income / Net sales) × 100 = (35,000 / 500,000) × 100 = 7%.
This means 7 cents of each sales dollar is profit.
